brief_item.title: PASTE：并行工具执行与LLM生成的低延迟Agent服务系统
brief_item.core_conclusion: LLM Agent的生成-工具执行串行回路使工具时延完全暴露在任务关键路径上。PASTE通过预测未来工具调用并与LLM生成重叠执行，显著降低端到端任务时延。
brief_item.mechanism: PASTE从重复的Agent模式中预测具体的未来工具调用，在LLM仍在生成时推测执行这些调用，并在LLM确认前隔离推测结果；同时将工具执行与返回的LLM会话联合调度，避免瓶颈转移到GPU侧。
brief_item.result: 在深度研究、编程和科学Agent三类负载下，平均任务完成时间降低43.5%（基线：串行生成-执行回路的服务系统）。；观测到的工具时延降低1.8倍（条件：与LLM生成重叠的推测工具执行）。
brief_item.boundary: 结果仅来自arXiv摘要，全文未获取；增益依赖于可重复、可预测的Agent工具模式，预测器准确度与误推测代价在摘要中未量化；基线被笼统描述为“当今服务系统”，未指名对照系统。
brief_item.project_relevance: 判断：与Agent加速主题直接相关——将推测工具调用与LLM生成并行化，是与代码知识图、并行推测工具链互补的调度重叠技术；其对工具执行与返回LLM会话的联合调度，也关系到当一级并行化后瓶颈向GPU侧迁移的问题。

facts.title: Parallelizing Tool Execution and LLM Generation for Low-Latency Agent Serving (PASTE)
facts.event_hint: New agent-serving system that overlaps speculative tool execution with LLM generation to hide tool latency on the agent critical path.
facts.problem: LLM-powered agents run a sequential generation-then-tool-execution loop, and today's serving systems serialize it, leaving tool latency fully exposed on the task critical path.
facts.mechanism: PASTE predicts concrete future tool invocations from recurring agent patterns and speculatively executes them while the LLM is still generating; it isolates speculative results until confirmed by the LLM, and jointly schedules tool execution with returning LLM sessions to avoid shifting bottlenecks onto the GPU.

evidence.claim: Average task completion time reduced by 43.5% across deep research, coding, and scientific-agent workloads.
evidence.baseline: today's serving systems that serialize the generation-execution loop
evidence.condition: deep research, coding, and scientific-agent workloads
speculative tool execution overlapped with LLM generation

facts.evaluation_context: Three agent workload categories: deep research, coding, and scientific agents. Comparison is against conventional serving systems that serialize the model-generation and tool-execution loop.
facts.limitations: Abstract-level only; full body not fetched. Gains depend on recurring/predictable agent tool patterns; the accuracy of the invocation predictor and mis-speculation costs are not quantified in the abstract. Baselines are described generically as 'today's serving systems' without a named system.
facts.project_relevance: Directly relevant to Agent acceleration: it parallelizes speculative tool calls with LLM generation, a scheduling/overlap technique that complements code-graph and parallel-speculative tooling themes. The joint scheduling of tool execution and returning LLM sessions also intersects with GPU-side inference-network/TPN concerns about where bottlenecks move when one stage is parallelized.
